text: Running stitch: align the cloth and pass a threaded needle alternately up and down through it at regular intervals along the seam line. On a stable woven fabric, pick up several small stitches before pulling the thread through. Keep the tension just taut enough to lie flat; pulling harder turns the seam into gathers.

text: For a continuous hand-sewn line, bring the needle up one stitch ahead of the starting point. Insert it back at the start and bring it up one stitch beyond its previous exit. Repeat, returning each insertion to the preceding exit point. Uniform stitch lengths make the visible line continuous while the reverse side overlaps.
provenance: Original procedure paraphrase; Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework, Plain Sewing, figures 4–22; public-domain primary craft manual, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/20776/pg20776-images.html . Wording and practical dimensions adapted, not copied.

text: To enclose a raw fabric edge, fold it inward once, then fold again so the cut edge lies inside the fold. Secure with small slanting hemming stitches that catch the fold and only a little of the underlying cloth. Baste a wide hem first so its depth stays consistent while sewing.
provenance: Original procedure paraphrase; Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework, Plain Sewing, figures 4–22; public-domain primary craft manual, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/20776/pg20776-images.html . Wording and practical dimensions adapted, not copied.

text: Flat-fell a seam by joining two aligned edges, then trimming one seam allowance narrower than the other. Fold the wider allowance over the narrow one, turn its raw edge under, and hem it to the cloth. Smooth as you work so the enclosed allowances lie flat instead of forming a bulge.
provenance: Original procedure paraphrase; Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework, Plain Sewing, figures 4–22; public-domain primary craft manual, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/20776/pg20776-images.html . Wording and practical dimensions adapted, not copied.

text: Make a fine rolled seam by backstitching two aligned fabric edges, trimming the inner allowance very narrow, and rolling the outer allowance around it. Secure the roll with hemming stitches as you advance. The raw edge stays enclosed and the reverse of the seam resembles a slender cord.
provenance: Original procedure paraphrase; Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework, Plain Sewing, figures 4–22; public-domain primary craft manual, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/20776/pg20776-images.html . Wording and practical dimensions adapted, not copied.

text: To join two finished selvedges by over-sewing, pin or baste them in alignment. Work small, closely spaced stitches through both edges, taking up only a little cloth. Do not tighten the thread enough to ridge the join: the two selvedges should lie side by side when the seam is opened flat.
provenance: Original procedure paraphrase; Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework, Plain Sewing, figures 4–22; public-domain primary craft manual, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/20776/pg20776-images.html . Wording and practical dimensions adapted, not copied.

text: A French seam encloses fraying edges in two passes. First sew with wrong sides together and trim the allowances narrow. Fold at that seam with right sides together, then sew a second seam wide enough to contain both trimmed edges. Check that loose threads are enclosed before finishing the second pass.
provenance: Original procedure paraphrase; Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework, Plain Sewing, figures 4–22; public-domain primary craft manual, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/20776/pg20776-images.html . Wording and practical dimensions adapted, not copied.

text: Run a gathering thread along the cloth, draw it up, and distribute the folds evenly. Divide both the gathered length and its receiving band into equal sections, then pin corresponding marks together. Sew the gathers to the band with their fullness evenly distributed; matching endpoints alone would allow bunching in the middle.
provenance: Original procedure paraphrase; Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework, Plain Sewing, figures 4–22; public-domain primary craft manual, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/20776/pg20776-images.html . Wording and practical dimensions adapted, not copied.

text: After arranging gathers along a first running thread, sew a second parallel gathering row below it. Pull both threads evenly and align the folds between the rows. The paired rows stabilize the fullness and help the gathered edge stay straight while it is attached to another piece.
provenance: Original procedure paraphrase; Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework, Plain Sewing, figures 4–22; public-domain primary craft manual, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/20776/pg20776-images.html . Wording and practical dimensions adapted, not copied.

text: For gathering a very fine fabric edge, roll the edge into a narrow tube between thumb and finger. Pass small stitches from the inside to the outside of the roll at regular intervals. Draw the thread up gently as you proceed; the roll encloses the edge while the thread forms the gathers.
provenance: Original procedure paraphrase; Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework, Plain Sewing, figures 4–22; public-domain primary craft manual, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/20776/pg20776-images.html . Wording and practical dimensions adapted, not copied.

text: To introduce a new thread into running stitch or backstitch without a bulky knot, make its first stitch, lay the old and new thread ends along the next part of the seam, and work the following stitches over both ends. The stitched overlap secures the join inside the work.
provenance: Original procedure paraphrase; Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework, Plain Sewing, figures 4–22; public-domain primary craft manual, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/20776/pg20776-images.html . Wording and practical dimensions adapted, not copied.

text: Mark a straight stitching line by following the fabric’s woven threads when possible. For a diagonal line or material whose threads cannot be drawn, run a contrasting temporary basting thread as a guide. Sew consistently along it, then remove the guide after the permanent stitches are secure.
